parole.testo: From the 1860s. Origin unknown. Perhaps from Igbo bem (“my home, household, folk, fellows”).

parole.significato: A chief of the Igbo people.

parole.testo: Borrowed from Igbo gbam. Formed entirely from the Igbo alphabet (Ábídíị), utilizing the native compound consonant digraph "gb", along with "a" and "m". Originally an Igbo ideophone, it has been widely adopted into contemporary Nigerian English and Pidgin as a universal slang term.

parole.significato: The belief of reincarnation in Odinani.
parole.testo: From Igbo inouwa (“come back to the world”)

parole.significato: A spicy Nigerian dish made from a goat's head.
A string of beads worn around the waist by Nigerian women.

parole.testo: Evidently from Igbo Kanye, although inspiration from other African languages may have contributed. The verb is a reference to Kanye West interrupting Taylor Swift’s speech at the 2009 MTV Video Music Awards.

parole.significato: A traditional masquerade of the Igbo people.
parole.testo: From Igbo ḿmánwụ́ (“spirit of the dead”), from ḿmuo (“spirit”) + ọnwụ (“death”).

parole.significato: A spicy Nigerian dish made from cow foot.
A form of folk magic, medicine or witchcraft originating in Africa and practised in parts of the Caribbean.
parole.testo: Uncertain; apparently from a Caribbean creole, probably ultimately from a West African language. The Oxford English Dictionary points to Igbo abià (“knowledge, wisdom”), obìa (“doctor, healer”). Cognate of Aukan obiya, Saramaccan obia, and Sranan Tongo obia.

parole.significato: In Igbo folklore, an evil spirit that is born into a family to bring them misfortune.
The almond-like seeds of Irvingia gabonensis, used to thicken soup, etc.
The edible immature mucilaginous seed pod (properly, capsule) of the Abelmoschus esculentus.
parole.testo: From an unknown West African language, probably Igbo ọ́kụ̀rụ̀ but cf. Akan ŋkrũmã and ŋkrakra (“broth”).

parole.significato: Any of various large, colourful, deep-bodied pelagic fish of the family Lamprididae.
parole.testo: From Igbo uba. parole.significato: An informal money pooling scheme practised in Africa, the Caribbean, and some immigrant communities.
parole.testo: Possibly from West African Igbo isusu / esusu (“pooling the funds”) or Yoruba esúsú (“revolving loan fund”).

parole.significato: A jug-shaped percussion instrument of Igbo origin.
You (plural); y'all, you guys, you all.
parole.testo: From Igbo ụnụ. Compare Jamaican Creole unnu.
